WP OPS - WordPress Operations Handbook
Book TOC Ideas Foundations

EBOOK IDEAS

Goal: make this repository read like an ebook while staying practical for operators.

Suggested book structure

  • Front matter: title page, edition, changelog link, how to use this book.
  • Part I: Foundations (stack overview, safety rules, environment setup).
  • Part II: Core workflows (provision, deploy, backups, restores, monitoring).
  • Part III: Operations playbook (incidents, migrations, performance).
  • Part IV: Advanced topics (multi-env, scaling, security hardening).
  • Appendices: glossary, command reference, troubleshooting index.

Concrete changes to make it feel like an ebook

  • Add a BOOK.md or TOC.md with a curated reading path and chapter order.
  • Use consistent chapter numbering in headings (e.g., “Chapter 3: Backups”).
  • Add short chapter intros with goals, prerequisites, and time estimates.
  • Include “Key takeaways” and “Next steps” at the end of each chapter.
  • Create sidebars for “Caution”, “Tip”, and “Gotcha” blocks.
  • Add a glossary that defines Trellis, Bedrock, vault, etc.
  • Add a command index: “ansible-playbook”, “wp”, “rsync”, “ssh”.
  • Use consistent diagrams (Mermaid) for flows and architecture.

Mapping existing docs into a book

  • README.md becomes the “Preface” and “How to use this book”.
  • trellis/, wp-cli/, and nginx/ become core chapters with sub-sections.
  • troubleshooting/ becomes an appendix indexed by symptoms.
  • CHANGELOG.md becomes “Edition history”.

Chapter template (example)

  • Title and purpose
  • Prerequisites
  • Safety checklist
  • Step-by-step workflow (with dry-run first)
  • Verification steps
  • Cleanup / rollback
  • Troubleshooting notes
  • References / related chapters

Reading paths

  • “New operator”: setup -> backups -> monitoring -> incident response
  • “Migration”: inventory -> backup -> dry-run -> cutover -> verify
  • “Performance”: caching -> image optimization -> monitoring

Visual and format ideas

  • Add callout styling using Markdown blockquotes with labels.
  • Use diagrams to show data flow and failure points.
  • Provide “before/after” snippets for config changes.
  • Include small, realistic case studies for each major workflow.
  • Add periodic “You should know” recap sections.

Tooling options (if desired)

  • Generate a static ebook with mdBook or MkDocs.
  • Keep markdown as the source of truth; export to PDF/EPUB.
  • Use a docs/ build step later, but keep repo structure intact.

Next candidate chapters to write

  • Chapter: Safe backup and restore (Trellis + wp-cli).
  • Chapter: Deployment checklist and rollback.
  • Chapter: Monitoring signals and alert triage.
  • Chapter: Image optimization pipeline.

  <h1>PR Helper Script</h1>

  

  <h1 id="create-pr-script">Create PR Script</h1>

<p>An intelligent script (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">create-pr.sh</code>) that creates GitHub pull requests with professional, AI-powered descriptions similar to GitHub Copilot.</p>

<h2 id="features">Features</h2>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Multi-AI Backend Support</strong>: Choose between Claude CLI or Codex CLI for AI-powered descriptions</li>
  <li><strong>AI-Powered Descriptions</strong>: Uses AI to analyze git diffs and generate intelligent summaries</li>
  <li><strong>Professional Formatting</strong>: Creates descriptions with grouped sections, bold headings, and detailed bullet points</li>
  <li><strong>Clickable File Links</strong>: Each file links directly to the changed version on GitHub for quick access</li>
  <li><strong>Smart Categorization</strong>: Automatically detects change types (dependencies, documentation, styling, etc.)</li>
  <li><strong>Automatic PR Creation</strong>: Uses GitHub CLI to create the actual pull request</li>
  <li><strong>Fallback Mode</strong>: Works without AI when API key is not available</li>
  <li><strong>Interactive AI Selection</strong>: Choose your preferred AI tool when both are available</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="token-usage-comparison">Token Usage Comparison</h2>

<p>Understanding the cost/benefit of using AI vs no-AI mode:</p>

<h3 id="option-1-claude-code-without-this-script-manual-pr">Option 1: Claude Code without this script (Manual PR)</h3>
<p><strong>Token Usage</strong>: ~2,000-10,000+ tokens per PR</p>
<ul>
  <li>You ask Claude: “Create a PR for my changes”</li>
  <li>Claude reads multiple files to understand context</li>
  <li>Back-and-forth conversation to refine the description</li>
  <li>Claude runs git commands to analyze changes</li>
  <li><strong>Result</strong>: Uses significant tokens, quality depends on conversation</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="option-2-this-script-with-ai---no-ai-not-used">Option 2: This Script with AI (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--no-ai</code> NOT used)</h3>
<p><strong>Token Usage</strong>: ~500-1,500 tokens per PR</p>
<ul>
  <li>Script pre-processes all git data (commits, files, diff stats)</li>
  <li>Sends only structured summary to Claude</li>
  <li>Single prompt, no back-and-forth needed</li>
  <li>Claude generates description in one response</li>
  <li><strong>Result</strong>: 70-85% fewer tokens than manual, high-quality output</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="option-3-this-script-without-ai---no-ai-flag">Option 3: This Script without AI (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--no-ai</code> flag)</h3>
<p><strong>Token Usage</strong>: 0 tokens</p>
<ul>
  <li>Script generates basic but professional description</li>
  <li>Lists all commits, files changed, and statistics</li>
  <li>No intelligent grouping or summarization</li>
  <li><strong>Result</strong>: Free, but generic descriptions</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="recommendation">Recommendation</h3>

<p><strong>Use Script + AI</strong> when:</p>
<ul>
  <li>You want Copilot-quality descriptions</li>
  <li>You want to save 70-85% tokens vs manual</li>
  <li>The PR has complex changes that need explanation</li>
  <li>You want consistent, professional output</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Use Script –no-ai</strong> when:</p>
<ul>
  <li>The PR is simple (e.g., dependency update, single file change)</li>
  <li>You don’t need intelligent summarization</li>
  <li>You want zero token usage</li>
  <li>You’ll manually edit the description anyway</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="prerequisites">Prerequisites</h2>

<ol>
  <li><strong>GitHub CLI</strong> (required)
    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>brew <span class="nb">install </span>gh
gh auth login
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p><strong>AI CLI</strong> (optional, for AI descriptions)</p>

    <p>Choose one or both:</p>

    <p><strong>Claude CLI</strong> (recommended)</p>
    <ul>
      <li>If you’re using Claude Code in VS Code, you already have this installed!</li>
      <li>Otherwise, download from: https://claude.ai/download</li>
      <li>The script will automatically use your existing Claude authentication</li>
    </ul>

    <p><strong>Codex CLI</strong> (alternative)</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Install via npm: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">npm install -g @anthropic-ai/codex-cli</code></li>
      <li>Or download from your AI provider</li>
    </ul>

    <p>The script automatically detects which AI tools are available and lets you choose interactively.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<h2 id="installation">Installation</h2>

<ol>
  <li>Make the script executable:
    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nb">chmod</span> +x create-pr.sh
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>Optionally, add to your PATH or create an alias:
    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc</span>

</code></pre></div>    </div>

<h2 id="usage">Usage</h2>

<h3 id="interactive-mode-default">Interactive Mode (Default)</h3>

<p>Just run the script and answer the prompts:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>./create-pr.sh

<span class="c"># You'll be prompted for:</span>
<span class="c"># 1. Base branch (default: main)</span>
<span class="c"># 2. PR title (default: auto-generated from branch name)</span>
<span class="c"># 3. Use AI for description? (Y/n)</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><strong>Example interaction:</strong></p>
<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>🚀 Create Pull Request
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Current branch: feature/user-auth

Base branch (default: main):
PR title (default: Feature User Auth): Add user authentication
Use AI to generate description? (Y/n): y

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="non-interactive-mode">Non-Interactive Mode</h3>

<p>Provide arguments to skip prompts:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># With all arguments</span>
./create-pr.sh main <span class="s2">"Add authentication feature"</span>

<span class="c"># Just base branch (title auto-generated)</span>
./create-pr.sh develop

<span class="c"># Skip all prompts, use defaults</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--no-interactive</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="options">Options</h3>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Choose AI backend (claude or codex)</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--ai</span><span class="o">=</span>claude
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--ai</span><span class="o">=</span>codex

<span class="c"># Skip AI generation (0 tokens, basic description)</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--no-ai</span>

<span class="c"># Skip all prompts, use arguments/defaults</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--no-interactive</span>

<span class="c"># Combine options</span>
./create-pr.sh main <span class="s2">"Feature update"</span> <span class="nt">--ai</span><span class="o">=</span>codex <span class="nt">--no-interactive</span>
./create-pr.sh main <span class="s2">"Feature update"</span> <span class="nt">--no-ai</span> <span class="nt">--no-interactive</span>

<span class="c"># Update existing PR with fresh AI-generated description</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--update</span>
./create-pr.sh <span class="nt">--update</span> <span class="nt">--ai</span><span class="o">=</span>codex
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="summary-of-differences">Summary of Differences</h3>

<p><strong>AI Mode advantages:</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>Explains WHY changes were made, not just WHAT</li>
  <li>Groups related changes with meaningful headings</li>
  <li>Extracts specific details (version numbers, security features)</li>
  <li>Provides context for reviewers</li>
  <li>Looks like a senior developer wrote it</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>No-AI Mode advantages:</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>Zero token cost</li>
  <li>Instant generation</li>
  <li>Still includes all file links and commit messages</li>
  <li>Good for simple PRs or when you’ll edit manually</li>
  <li>Professional structure, just less intelligent</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="how-it-works">How It Works</h2>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Branch Detection</strong>: Automatically detects current branch and ensures it’s pushed to remote</li>
  <li><strong>Change Analysis</strong>: Collects commits, file changes, and diff statistics</li>
  <li><strong>Category Detection</strong>: Identifies change types based on file patterns</li>
  <li><strong>AI Generation</strong> (if enabled): Sends context to Claude API for intelligent summary</li>
  <li><strong>PR Creation</strong>: Uses <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">gh pr create</code> to create the actual GitHub pull request</li>
</ol>

<h2 id="ai-description-generation">AI Description Generation</h2>

<p>When an AI CLI is available (Claude or Codex), the script:</p>

<ol>
  <li>Analyzes commit messages, changed files, and categories</li>
  <li>Sends a structured prompt to your chosen AI tool using your existing authentication</li>
  <li>Receives a professional description with:
    <ul>
      <li>Concise introductory paragraph</li>
      <li>Grouped sections with bold headings</li>
      <li>Detailed bullet points</li>
      <li>Specific metrics and version numbers</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ol>

<p>The AI is instructed to write like a senior developer - no emoticons, professional tone, focusing on what changed and why.</p>

<h3 id="choosing-your-ai-backend">Choosing Your AI Backend</h3>

<p>The script supports multiple AI backends:</p>

<p><strong>Automatic Detection</strong>: If you don’t specify <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ai=</code>, the script will:</p>
<ol>
  <li>Check for both Claude and Codex CLIs</li>
  <li>If both are available, ask you to choose</li>
  <li>If only one is available, use that automatically</li>
  <li>If none are available, offer no-AI mode</li>
</ol>

<p><strong>Manual Selection</strong>: Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ai=claude</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ai=codex</code> to force a specific backend</p>

<p><strong>Interactive Selection</strong>: When both are available and you’re in interactive mode:</p>
<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>Available AI tools: claude codex
Choose AI tool [default: claude]: codex
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="environment-variables">Environment Variables</h3>

<p>For advanced users, you can customize the CLI commands and arguments:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c"># Use custom Claude command name</span>
<span class="nb">export </span><span class="nv">CLAUDE_COMMAND</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"claude-custom"</span>

<span class="c"># Use custom Codex command name</span>
<span class="nb">export </span><span class="nv">CODEX_COMMAND</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"my-codex"</span>

<span class="c"># Pass custom arguments to Claude CLI</span>
<span class="nb">export </span><span class="nv">CLAUDE_CLI_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"--model=opus --timeout=30"</span>

<span class="c"># Pass custom arguments to Codex CLI</span>
<span class="nb">export </span><span class="nv">CODEX_CLI_ARGS</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">"--verbose"</span>

./create-pr.sh
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><strong>Note</strong>: If you’re using Claude Code in VS Code, the Claude CLI works automatically with no additional setup!</p>

<h2 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</h2>

<h3 id="no-ai-cli-found">“No AI CLI found”</h3>

<p>The script checks for both <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">claude</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">codex</code> commands. If neither is found:</p>

<p><strong>For Claude CLI:</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>If you’re using Claude Code in VS Code, make sure the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">claude</code> command is in your PATH:
    <div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>which claude
<span class="c"># Should output: /Users/yourname/.volta/bin/claude</span>
</code></pre></div>    </div>
  </li>
  <li>Restart your terminal after installing Claude Code</li>
  <li>Download Claude CLI from: https://claude.ai/download</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>For Codex CLI:</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>Install via npm: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">npm install -g @anthropic-ai/codex-cli</code></li>
  <li>Or check your AI provider’s installation instructions</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Workaround:</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li>Run with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--no-ai</code> flag to skip AI generation and use basic descriptions</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="ai-tool-codex-not-found">“AI tool ‘codex’ not found”</h3>

<p>If you specified <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ai=codex</code> but don’t have it installed:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Remove the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--ai=codex</code> flag to use Claude (if available)</li>
  <li>Install Codex CLI</li>
  <li>Or use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--no-ai</code> for basic descriptions</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="gh-is-not-installed">“gh is not installed”</h3>

<p>Install with: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">brew install gh</code> and authenticate with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">gh auth login</code></p>

<h3 id="pr-creation-fails">PR creation fails</h3>

<p>Make sure:</p>
<ul>
  <li>You’re on a feature branch (not main/master)</li>
  <li>Your branch is pushed to remote</li>
  <li>You’re authenticated with GitHub CLI</li>
</ul>

8. Code Block Enhancements

Add copy-to-clipboard functionality for code blocks:

<!-- Add to _layouts/default.html before </body> -->
<script>
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
    document.querySelectorAll('pre code').forEach(function(block) {
      const button = document.createElement('button');
      button.className = 'copy-button';
      button.textContent = 'Copy';
      button.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Copy code to clipboard');

      block.parentElement.style.position = 'relative';
      block.parentElement.appendChild(button);

      button.addEventListener('click', function() {
        navigator.clipboard.writeText(block.textContent).then(function() {
          button.textContent = 'Copied!';
          setTimeout(function() {
            button.textContent = 'Copy';
          }, 2000);
        });
      });
    });
  });
</script>

Dark mode JavaScript:

<script>
  const toggle = document.getElementById('theme-toggle');
  const currentTheme = localStorage.getItem('theme') || 'light';
  document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', currentTheme);

  toggle.addEventListener('click', function() {
    const theme = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme');
    const newTheme = theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', newTheme);
    localStorage.setItem('theme', newTheme);
  });
</script>
